title: Drink water before one meal
tip: Have a glass of water before one meal today.
why: Hydration can support better eating decisions and may reduce mindless snacking or overeating.
try_today: Drink a glass of water 10 minutes before lunch or dinner.

title: Swap the side
tip: Replace one starchy side with vegetables today.
why: Reducing the starch load of a meal may help reduce a large post-meal rise.
try_today: Choose extra vegetables instead of fries or extra rice.

title: Choose berries more often
tip: Use berries as a lighter sweet option.
why: Berries are often lower in sugar per serving than many desserts and sweet snacks.
try_today: Add a small serving of berries to plain yogurt instead of having cake or biscuits.

title: Add vegetables to eggs
tip: Boost breakfast with vegetables if you are having eggs.
why: Adding vegetables increases fiber and volume without adding many fast-digesting carbs.
try_today: Add spinach, peppers, onions, or mushrooms to eggs.

title: Choose plain yogurt
tip: Pick plain yogurt and add your own toppings.
why: Flavored yogurts often contain added sugars that make the total carb load higher.
try_today: Use plain yogurt with cinnamon and berries instead of sweetened yogurt.

title: Prioritize protein at lunch
tip: Make sure lunch includes a meaningful protein source.
why: A balanced lunch may reduce afternoon cravings and energy swings.
try_today: Add chicken, tuna, tofu, eggs, yogurt, or beans to lunch.

title: Add fiber at breakfast
tip: Start the day with extra fiber.
why: Fiber can slow digestion and help keep breakfast more balanced.
try_today: Add chia, flax, berries, or vegetables to breakfast.

title: Boost oats with protein
tip: If you eat oats, add protein or healthy fat.
why: This can help make the meal steadier than oats alone.
try_today: Add Greek yogurt, nuts, seeds, or peanut butter to oats.

title: Leave the starch until later in the meal
tip: Eat the starchier part of the meal after protein and vegetables.
why: Meal order may affect the speed of post-meal glucose rise.
try_today: Eat your protein and vegetables before the rice, bread, or pasta.

title: Pair coffee with food
tip: If coffee leaves you shaky or hungry, have it with food.
why: Some people feel better when caffeine is paired with a balanced meal.
try_today: Have coffee with breakfast instead of by itself.

title: Check the bread label
tip: Choose bread with more fiber and less added sugar when possible.
why: Higher-fiber bread is often a gentler choice than very refined bread.
try_today: Compare two bread labels and choose the higher-fiber option.

title: Watch sweet breakfasts
tip: Avoid making breakfast mostly sugar and refined carbs.
why: Sweet breakfasts can lead to a sharper early glucose rise and earlier hunger.
try_today: Swap pastry or sweet cereal for eggs, yogurt, oats with protein, or toast with eggs.

title: Pair rice with beans
tip: If you are having rice, pair it with beans or another protein source.
why: Mixing starch with protein and fiber may make the meal more balanced.
try_today: Add beans, lentils, fish, chicken, or tofu to a rice-based meal.

title: Start dinner with a salad
tip: Have salad or vegetables before the rest of dinner.
why: Starting with fiber can help shift the meal toward a steadier glucose response.
try_today: Eat salad, cucumber, or lightly cooked vegetables before the main course.

title: Do not eat in a rush

why: Rushed eating can make portion awareness harder.
try_today: Sit down and give one meal your full attention for 15 minutes.
